unruled:gate:ftc.has_tax.class: no gate defect; findings on the condition's own question, pre-existing
unruled:gate:ftc.has_tax.reason: The gate is a C gate on ftc.has_tax (ftc.taxes above zero), which the credit already read: before the gate ftc.needs1116 was all[has_tax, ...] and ftc.credit took $0 without foreign tax, so the four election answers changed no value when ftc.taxes is zero (every fixture's recorded value is unchanged). The findings concern who answers ftc.taxes zero wrongly. (1) K-1 (Form 1041) and K-3 (Form 1065, 1120-S) foreign tax: designed out; an estate, trust, partnership or S corporation interest is refused by scope.schedule1 ('partnerships, S corporations, estates or trusts (Schedule E or a Schedule K-1)'). (2) foreign tax paid directly or withheld with no payee statement: the help asks for 'Foreign income taxes you paid, after any required reductions. Usually the total of Form 1099-INT box 6 and Form 1099-DIV box 7', 'usually', not 'only', and such a filer needs Form 1116 (no qualified payee statement, i1116 p. 1), which scope.credits refuses ('any credit other than ... the foreign tax credit claimed without Form 1116'). (3) a carryover with no 2025 tax and (4) a redetermination for an earlier year: both are claimed on Form 1116 and its Schedules B and C (i1116 p. 2), refused by scope.credits; the gate changes nothing for them. (5) a filer unsure whether withheld tax is 'creditable': a wording point on ftc.taxes, low, unchanged by the gate. No finding shows a non-zero gated line under a false condition.

unruled:gate:f8889.dec_coverage.class: no gate defect; findings on the condition's own question, pre-existing
unruled:gate:f8889.dec_coverage.reason: The gate hides f8889.last_month when f8889.dec_coverage is none: i8889 p. 2, Last-month rule, 'You may consider yourself an "eligible individual" for the entire year if you are an eligible individual on the 1st day of the last month of the tax year'. Before the gate f8889.use_last_month was all[dec_coverage != none, last_month], already false for none, so no value changed (every fixture's recorded value is unchanged). The findings concern who answers dec_coverage none wrongly, the condition's own pre-existing question: (1) a fiscal-year filer (high by the reviewer): the tool prepares calendar-year 2025 returns throughout and every form's dates assume it; no fiscal-year screen exists anywhere, a model-wide assumption reported to the owner, not a defect of this gate; (2) a spouse covered under the other spouse's family HDHP: the question already says to answer family for both spouses when either had family HDHP coverage and both were eligible (i8889 p. 4, Line 1); (3) disregarded coverage and (4) a plan not labelled HDHP: wording points on what an eligible individual is (i8889 p. 2), unchanged by the gate; (5) a spouse who died before December 1, low. No finding shows a non-zero gated line under a false condition.

unruled:gate:household.claims_8862_credi.class: no gate defect; the condition is exactly the claim the instructions name
unruled:gate:household.claims_8862_credi.reason: The gate asks household.credit_disallowed only when the return claims the earned income credit (Steps 1 to 5 passed and eic.line6, the credit of Worksheet A line 6 or Worksheet B line 11, above zero) or Schedule 8812 line 8 is more than line 11 (line 12, 'No. Stop here. You cannot take the child tax credit, credit for other dependents, or additional child tax credit'); i1040gi p. 39 and p. 43, Form 8862, who must file ('You must file Form 8862 to claim ...'). Before the gate both refusal gates (household.ctc_disallowed_claim, household.eic_disallowed_claim) already required the same claim, so no value of a fixture changes. (1, medium) A filer who has the IRS figure the earned income credit: the tool has no such election; it always figures the credit itself (eic.credit reads eic.line6), so the condition is the credit the return claims. (2, low) A credit computed as zero because of a wrong entry: the reviewer agrees no Form 8862 applies to a credit not claimed. The earlier rounds' findings on the question's wording were fixed before this review: the question now names the spouse on a joint return, and its help covers a credit on any earlier return either spouse filed (including a joint return with someone else), any reduction by notice, letter, audit or court decision or a refund issued without the credit, and 'If you are not sure, answer Yes'.

unruled:gate:s1.has_jury_pay.class: no gate defect; the condition is the owner-approved C gate on line 8h
unruled:gate:s1.has_jury_pay.reason: The gate asks s1.jury_to_employer only when Schedule 1 line 8h is above zero (design, question hierarchy: 'Jury pay given to your employer [C: only if jury pay (8h) is above zero]'). Line 24a is a part of line 8h: i1040gi p. 91, Line 8h, 'Enter any jury duty pay and see the instructions for line 24a'; p525 p. 34, Jury duty, 'Jury duty pay you receive must be included in your income on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8h. If you must give the pay to your employer ... you can deduct the amount turned over to your employer'; the chosen reading of amb.2025.jury_24a_cap treats an amount given above line 8h as an impossible entry. (1, high) Pay received and reported in 2024 and turned over in 2025: that is a repayment of an amount included in income in an earlier year, which p525 p. 36, Repayments, treats separately ('If you had to repay an amount that you included in your income in an earlier year, you may be able to deduct the amount repaid from your income for the year in which you repaid it'), not line 24a of the year of receipt; before the gate the tool asked the amount and refused it as an impossible entry (s1.jury_over), now it does not ask it. Neither handles a claim-of-right repayment, which no screen names; reported to the owner as an open question, not a gate defect. (2, medium) Jury pay entered as other income (line 8z or a Form 1099-MISC): line 8h is asked of every filer and p525 p. 34 puts jury pay on line 8h; its help now says 'All jury duty pay received in 2025, whether or not a form reported it, including any pay you gave to your employer'. (3, low) Pay signed over and never entered: the line 8h question and help both say to include pay given to the employer. Every fixture's recorded value is unchanged.

div.any lists money market funds; its help says fund amounts are dividends even when a statement calls them interest or tax-exempt interest.

unruled:gate:div.has_return_of_capital.reason: No defect of the gate: the gated answer is read only with box 3 above zero, as before the gate; the parent question names returns of capital and distributions without a form.

findings.evidence: div.any names 'nondividend distributions (a return of capital)' and 'dividends received without any form'; box 3 is asked whenever div.any is yes.
div.any names 'nondividend distributions (a return of capital)' among the distributions that count.
The box 3 question asks for the amount the form shows in box 3, not a taxable amount; a filer who leaves it out also leaves out the box from the forms combined. Low risk; no change.
The filer answers from the forms held; a later correction is an amended return.
